findings.summary: crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The plan ignores the reading as a source of changed rules, which the request and the accepted reading both require, and its stated reason is false.
findings.evidence: The request says "When a job's reading or diff changes a value or a stated behaviour". The reading's assumption says old values and claims come "from removed diff lines … and from decision-style claims in the reading". The plan rejects the reading because it is "not available at the candidate step of a resumed job". But `check_and_verify(&self, ctx, accepted: &AcceptedReading, …)` at mod.rs:1960-1964 receives the accepted reading, and `producer_loop` already reads `ctx.reading` (producer.rs:478). As planned, a job whose reading reverses a decided rule finds nothing unless the diff happens to remove a 6-word comment that repeats the decision word for word. Fix: Take claims from the accepted reading as well, for example its summary or criteria sentences that state the new rule. Search the log for the reverse or old form those sentences name, or at least for the decision ids and key terms they cite. Pass `accepted` at both call sites. Add a criterion-2 test where the changed rule comes from the reading and the diff has no removed comment.
findings.location: Plan decision 2 (Rejected: Read the accepted reading for claims); crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:1961

findings.summary: Treating any `older` id as marked exempts decisions that still stand, including the motivating ones (D08, D156).
findings.evidence: The decision-links.toml header defines `amended` as "the older decision is revised in part, or in prose only, and stays active". D156 is the older of D187 (lines 188-191, "D156 stands"). D08 is the older of D157 ("Amends D08 in prose only"). Under the plan's rule, a change that contradicts D08, which is exactly what job yvk0 did per D156's Case, is never reported, because some unrelated earlier entry amended it. `link_pairs` (decision_links.rs:101) drops the status, so the plan cannot tell these cases apart. Fix: Count a decision as marked only when its entry text says 'amended by' / 'superseded by', or when a link has status `superseded`, or when the link's `newer` entry is added by this change (the change reconciles it itself). Parse the status, or diff base and candidate links. Add a test where a decision that an older entry amended still gets reported.
findings.location: Plan decision 3 ('Marked' means … its id is the `older` of a [[link]]); docs/decision-links.toml:5-6, 186-191

findings.summary: Claims are taken from any removed line, so deleting or refactoring text fails jobs at the candidate even when no claim changed.
findings.evidence: A 'claim' is any removed comment line or non-table `.md` line of 6 or more words that is not re-added. Deleting a function, file or paragraph is not a reversed claim, yet any remaining copy of that text elsewhere becomes a hard failure (mod.rs block after 2020, after one send-back). The plan's only way out for a hit in an old decision is a link or phrase. The log is append-only and editing old entries is out of scope, so a false hit forces the producer to write a bogus 'Amends Dn' entry plus a link. D187 rejected failing jobs on a similar heuristic for this reason (decisions.md:5502-5503: "a false positive would block a job"). Fix: Take claims only from lines the change replaces (a removed line paired with a differing added line in the same hunk), not from pure deletions or deleted files. Add tests for a deleted function and a deleted file whose duplicated comments stay quiet. Alternatively, keep claim-only hits as send-back findings and close the job only on value hits and on claims from the reading, and say so in D190's Tradeoff.
findings.location: Plan approach (1) and decision 2: claims from removed comment or prose lines; Risks (false positives)

findings.summary: The plan misses a help string that restates a limit held in a named public constant, and that string is already stale.
findings.evidence: The `HestiaAction::Review` help (main.rs:572-574) says "The five highest-ranked causes (most occurrences, then most recent) are urgent, the rest normal." The enforcing constant is `pub const BACKFILL_HIGH: usize = 5` (hestia.rs:1494), documented as "How many of the highest-ranked causes a backfill makes high … Hestia never queues urgent", and used at hestia.rs:1924. Criterion 5 requires that "no literal copy of the limit remains in help text". The plan's survey says only plan, drain and check restate named constants. Fix: Add the hestia review help to the conversion: a `{backfill_high}` placeholder filled from `athena_core::hestia::BACKFILL_HIGH`, with 'urgent' corrected to 'high'. Add its template and filled-help tests. List it in Dependents. Re-survey every doc comment in main.rs against `pub const` limits instead of picking cases by hand.
findings.location: Plan decision 5 and step 7 (help strings converted: plan, drain, check only); crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs:570-574

findings.summary: The D190 rationale says D156's findings still reach the producer only on the next attempt, but the gate already runs in the loop.
findings.evidence: D187 says `decision_gate` "already runs in the producer loop and again at the candidate" (decisions.md:5487), and producer.rs:498 shows the call. D187's Tradeoff names the in-loop list follow-up (decisions.md:5506-5509). Saying this change "ends" D156's tradeoff would itself put a false claim into the log. Fix: In D190, cite D187's follow-up together with D156 (d). State only what is new: the stale-text list in the loop and help text filled from constants. Consider whether a D187 link is also needed.

findings.summary: A plain substring match on the phrase anywhere in an entry is loose.
findings.evidence: Any entry whose prose uses the words in another sense, for example "the list is amended by hand", would exempt the whole entry. The link-list header (decision-links.toml:12) defines the phrase form as "Superseded by <newer>", with an id. Fix: Require the phrase followed by a `D<n>` id, matching the parser's own phrase form in `athena_data::decision_links`.
findings.location: Plan decision 3 (entry contains 'amended by' or 'superseded by' in any case)

findings.summary: Other user-facing restatements of limits are neither converted nor listed.
findings.evidence: The drain after_help says "default 1" for `max_concurrency`; the default lives in a private `default_max_concurrency` (config.rs:286). display.rs:705 prints "one dispatch in three is Athena's own", which restates `IMPROVEMENT_GAP`. The plan converts that same phrase in main.rs but leaves the display copy literal. Fix: Either build the display.rs line from `IMPROVEMENT_GAP + 1`, or list both strings in the Rejected alternatives with the reason, so the scope choice is explicit.

summary: I read the code the plan cites and checked it. The plan uses the right places in the code. It hooks next to the decision gate in `producer_loop` (producer.rs:498-556), sends findings back through the shared send-back (`append_mirror_drift` pattern, send_back.rs:227), adds a closing failure after the candidate-step gate (mod.rs:2007-2020), and extends D156's placeholder fill in `cli_command()` (main.rs:605-623). The harness and git helpers it relies on exist: `governed_job_with`, `editing`, `commit_file`, `ls_tree`, `blob_sizes`, `cat_blobs`, `link_pairs` and `Snapshot::work_tree_tree`. The approach still has four major problems. (1) The request says "when a job's reading or diff changes" a rule, and the accepted reading takes claims from the reading. The plan drops the reading. Its reason is that the reading is not available at the candidate step, but `check_and_verify` receives `accepted: &AcceptedReading` (mod.rs:1961). (2) The plan counts a decision as "marked" when it is the `older` of any link. That exempts decisions that still stand: `amended` means the decision "stays active" (decision-links.toml:5-6). D08 and D156 are exempt today through D157 and D187, and D08 is the decision whose reversal motivated D156. (3) Claims come from every removed comment or prose line of 6 or more words. Deleting code or text then flags every duplicate of the deleted text, and the check fails the job at the candidate. A false hit in an old, append-only decision forces a bogus amending entry. (4) The help-string survey misses `athena hestia review --backfill` (main.rs:573). That help says "the five highest-ranked causes … are urgent", while `BACKFILL_HIGH = 5` makes them high and never urgent (hestia.rs:1492-1494, 1924). Criterion 5 would go unmet. Athena's main.rs scope finding is not repeated here. Verdict: revise.
